I've been working this land since I was a teenager, helping my father. Now it's mine — about 10 mu here in the plain south of Handan. The soil is decent loam, the water table is still reachable with my electric pump, though my neighbor says it's getting deeper every year.

I'm not going to change what works. Around here, everyone grows winter wheat then summer corn on the same fields. That's two harvests a year. I do the same. My father did it, the village committee promotes it, and the grain station buys it. Cotton prices have been bad, soybeans are fine but the yield money doesn't add up the same way. Wheat and corn it is.

For seed, I'll get the improved wheat variety from the township supply cooperative — probably Kenong 199 or whatever they have in stock that my neighbor used last year and got a good harvest. For corn I'll buy the hybrid bags,郑单958 or similar. I trust the dealer in town.

Fertilizer: I put down urea and diammonium phosphate, same as always. I put plenty on — more fertilizer, more grain, that's how I've always thought. I'll do a base application before wheat planting and a top-dress at jointing.

Water: I'll pump four times for the wheat — once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading, once when the grain is filling. For corn in summer I rely more on the rain but I'll pump once or twice if July is dry like last year.

I'll rotary till before planting wheat. For corn I just drill the seed right after I harvest the wheat — no time to plow, and it works fine.
